specifications.currentSnapshotAssessment: Existing gpa mode accepts numeric points/credits and previous GPA/credits; target planner exists. Letter/percentage transforms and term rows remain absent.
algorithmSteps: Label the default mapping Example 4.0 scale (editable); F is zero and P/NP are excluded in that specific example. Do not present it as a universal US or U-M policy.
Transform each included grade to numeric points. Percentage mode selects the row with largest minimumPercent <= grade; supplied thresholds, not a universal national scale, determine the result.
For each term compute qualityPoints=sum(points*credits), gradedCredits=sum(credits), termGpa=qualityPoints/gradedCredits. Excluded rows contribute to neither quantity.

Across terms sum quality points and graded credits before dividing. Add previousGpa*previousCredits to quality points and previousCredits to denominator. Never take an unweighted average of semester GPAs.
Keep full decimal precision until output formatting. Empty term GPA is unavailable, not zero; require some graded credit to calculate a cumulative result.
validation: Reject unknown grade symbols, negative credits, nonfinite values, an included row with zero credits, or points outside the configured maximum.
Require unique percentage cutoffs in [0,100], a zero cutoff, and finite points within scale maximum. Percentages above 100 need a separate explicit extra-credit policy.
Do not silently exclude failing grades, repeated courses, or transferred courses; these are institution-specific choices.

specifications.currentSnapshotAssessment: Count and add business days already exist with Mon–Fri plus one-off YYYY-MM-DD exclusions; recurring rules and selectable weekdays are absent.
algorithmSteps: Represent Gregorian civil dates as date-only values; no local timezone or DST arithmetic.
Generate selected fixed/nth-weekday/last-weekday rules for the range and adjacent years so a next-year New Year observation can fall in the previous December.
For observed-mon-fri fixed holidays move Saturday to Friday and Sunday to Monday. Label this fixed federal convention; it does not adapt automatically to a custom workweek.
Union and deduplicate generated exclusions, one-off dates and custom month/day dates. Invalid recurring Feb 29 is skipped in a nonleap year. Skip nonworking weekdays once, even if also holidays.

For counting preserve the existing signed start-inclusive/end-exclusive contract, with include-end available. For addition, do not count the starting date; zero leaves it unchanged; negative counts walk backward.

Apply current nationwide rules only for a clearly labeled supported range, suggested 2021–2099. Future dates are projections of rules verified in 2026; outside this range retain custom dates without implying historical federal accuracy.
validation: Require at least one working weekday. Validate every full date and month/day combination; reject Feb 30, permit recurring Feb 29.
Keep existing overall year/result bounds and span limits; never emit year 0 or malformed year 10000.
Do not default to including DC-only Inauguration Day; do not label Black Friday, Christmas Eve or New Year’s Eve nationwide federal holidays. They can be user-defined extras.

specifications.currentSnapshotAssessment: Current timesheet totals shifts then applies one weekly threshold; daily grouping, no-overtime selector and punch rounding are absent.

proposedFields.label: Round each clock punch to nearest

algorithmSteps: Parse times to integer seconds. An end earlier than the start belongs to the next day. Identical clock times mean a zero shift unless an explicit next-day flag is later added.
Round each absolute civil punch separately: rounded=q*floor((seconds+q/2)/q), q=roundMinutes*60. q=0 keeps it unchanged. A half-way tie moves to the later time. Preserve any midnight date carry.
Subtract the entered unpaid break duration after punch rounding; do not silently round the break itself. Retain raw and rounded net shift durations for comparison.

Aggregate net seconds by workDate before daily overtime. For this simple estimate, assign an overnight shift to its starting workDate and disclose that convention; it is not a legal payroll workday definition.
none: overtime=0. daily: sum(max(0,dayHours-threshold)). weekly: max(0,totalHours-threshold). regular=total-overtime. Do not sum daily and weekly overtime or double-count the same hours.
Pay=regular*rate+overtime*rate*multiplier; retain seconds/decimal precision until final pay formatting.
validation: Require an explicit day/date identifier for daily mode. Aggregate multiple rows belonging to the same day before applying threshold.
Reject negative breaks and breaks exceeding the rounded span; reject overlapping rows on the same civil timeline to avoid accidental double-counting.
Do not treat these configurable arithmetic modes as a complete wage-law engine; paid-break rules, exemptions, state rules, DST shifts and split overnight workdays require more inputs.

specifications.currentSnapshotAssessment: Existing mode is room-area/tile-area with waste and cost per tile. No direct area, grout, box or price-basis fields.
algorithmSteps: Convert all lengths to the same exact decimal unit. Tile orientation follows the entered length/width; do not imply optimal rotation or reuse of cut pieces.

Straight-grid mode with only internal joints: columns=ceil((roomLength+gap)/(tileLength+gap)), rows=ceil((roomWidth+gap)/(tileWidth+gap)), baseTiles=rows*columns. This is a stated layout model, not an inferred competitor algorithm.

Area-estimate mode with zero grout uses equivalentTiles=coverageArea/(tileLength*tileWidth). With nonzero grout it may offer equivalentTiles=coverageArea/((tileLength+gap)*(tileWidth+gap)), explicitly labeled periodic-module approximation; it cannot determine exact edge cuts from area alone.
Grid ordering: orderTiles=ceil(baseTiles*(1+waste/100)). Area ordering: orderTiles=ceil(equivalentTiles*(1+waste/100)); do not round equivalentTiles before applying waste.
boxes=ceil(orderTiles/tilesPerBox), purchasedTiles=boxes*tilesPerBox. Box-based purchasing applies these quantities; individual-tile purchasing can use orderTiles directly.

Price basis tile: purchased tile count*price; box: boxes*price; purchased-material-area: purchasedTileCount*tileLength*tileWidth*pricePerNormalizedArea. Show needed versus purchased quantities and package surplus.
validation: Lengths/tile dimensions must be positive, grout/waste/price nonnegative, box size a positive integer.
For known area, do not label the periodic grout estimate an exact layout count. Reject straight-grid mode without room dimensions.
Use decimal/rational ceiling to preserve exact-fit boundaries; an arbitrary floating epsilon can undercount genuinely larger rooms.
No default construction-code claims or guaranteed coverage for diagonal patterns, irregular rooms, lippage, damaged tiles or contractor cut plans.

specifications.currentSnapshotAssessment: Existing colors mode decodes four bands with limited tolerance options; conductor and network modes already exist.
algorithmSteps: Use two significant digits for 3/4 bands and three for 5/6 bands; resistance=significand*multiplier.
Three bands imply the absent tolerance band, ±20%. Four/five/six read the chosen verified tolerance color.
Minimum and maximum resistance are nominal*(1±tolerance/100). Six-band output adds the selected temperature-coefficient class in ppm/K.
Temperature coefficient is a magnitude/class label, not a measured signed linear response. Do not infer exact resistance at temperature from the band alone.
validation: Validate each role against its own allowed color table; digits cannot be gold or silver.

The lookup alone does not prove a physical marking convention. Do not invent a universal ban on a leading black digit; allow mathematical decoding with a manufacturer-check note for unusual leading-zero/all-zero markings. A single black-band zero-ohm link is a separate marking.
Do not decode a military failure-rate band as temperature coefficient. Do not invent tolerance values for unsupported orange/yellow/white colors.

specifications.currentSnapshotAssessment: Current metric and US tabs couple distance, consumption and price units; km/L and L/mile are absent.
algorithmSteps: Normalize distanceKm=distance for km or distance*1.609344 for miles.
Normalize litersPerKm: L/100km => economy/100; km/L => 1/economy; US-mpg => 3.785411784/(1.609344*economy); L/mi => economy/1.609344.
Normalize pricePerLiter: per-L => price; per-US-gal => price/3.785411784.
fuelLiters=distanceKm*litersPerKm, cost=fuelLiters*pricePerLiter, fuelUsGallons=fuelLiters/3.785411784. Currency changes the display label only; no exchange-rate conversion is performed.
validation: Reject nonpositive economy even if distance is zero, to keep mode transformations defined; distance and price may be zero.
Always distinguish US gallons from imperial gallons. UK mpg would be an explicitly added option, not a reinterpretation of the observed US-mpg field.

specifications.currentSnapshotAssessment: Current mode forces lower/upper/digits and optionally symbols. Existing inject-one-per-class then shuffle meets class membership but is not uniform over all class-valid strings.
algorithmSteps: Define disjoint ASCII pools for each selected class and state the exact symbol/ambiguous sets. Apply exclusions to pools before validation. Require each selected class to appear in a returned password, preserving existing behavior.
Use crypto.getRandomValues and rejection sampling for an unbiased integer index. For byte sampling and pool size n<=256, accept byte b < floor(256/n)*n, then index=b%n.

Without uniqueness, draw the whole candidate uniformly from the combined pool. Reject and regenerate candidates missing a required class; conditional on acceptance this is uniform over all permitted strings.
With uniqueness, securely Fisher–Yates shuffle the pool, take the required prefix, then reject candidates missing required classes. This is uniform over permitted ordered distinct-character strings.
Use a bounded retry cap and report an explicit failure if exceeded; never fall back to Math.random. Do not substitute mandatory-character injection while claiming uniform valid-password sampling.

Never derive an exact password fixture from product output. Test lengths, allowed sets, uniqueness and required class membership, plus deterministic random-index boundary tests with an injected test-only byte source.
validation: At least one class must remain selected and nonempty after exclusions. Length must be at least the number of required nonempty classes.
For no-repeat mode require length <= total available characters. Bound count and length as current mode does.
Do not log, persist, send to analytics, URL-encode or auto-copy generated secrets. Render as text, not markup.

specifications.currentSnapshotAssessment: IPv4 and IPv6 CIDR modes exist. IPv4 accepts prefix integer only; equivalent dotted-decimal mask input is absent.
algorithmSteps: Strictly parse address and dotted mask as exactly four decimal octets from 0 to 255. Reject signs, empty components, exponents and hex. Leading-zero policy should be explicit; strict unambiguous decimal without leading zeros is suggested.
As unsigned 32-bit BigInt M, let H=(~M)&0xffffffffn. A contiguous mask satisfies (H & (H+1n))===0n, including /0 and /32.
Obtain hostBits as bit length of H; prefix=32-hostBits. Reuse the existing IPv4 engine with that prefix instead of duplicating network arithmetic.
Return both prefix and dotted mask with network, total range, broadcast where meaningful and usable endpoints under the existing /31 point-to-point and /32 single-host convention.
validation: Reject discontiguous masks and invalid octets. Do not use signed JS bitwise values directly in displayed addresses.
Keep /31 point-to-point semantics explicitly labeled; a host count is a convention, not a guarantee that every address is routable or assignable in all networks.
